# Findly

> Findly is a free, open-source macOS menu bar utility. Press ⌃` to slide a Finder-style file drawer in from any screen edge; switch to another app and it automatically parks off-screen. It is its own window — not the real Finder — so it appears on every Space with a single line of collectionBehavior, with no Apple Events, Accessibility, or private SPI.

- Platform: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later
- Price: Free, open source (MIT license)
- Author: rocavence (https://github.com/rocavence)
- Download: https://github.com/rocavence/Findly-app/releases/latest
- Source code: https://github.com/rocavence/Findly-app
- Website: https://findly.rocavence.com

## What it does

Findly is a quick file drawer you can summon over anything and dismiss just as fast:

- Press ⌃` to slide the drawer in/out; use ⌃⌥ + arrow keys to summon it to the top, bottom, left, or right edge.
- It appears on whichever screen the mouse is on.
- Switch to another app and the drawer auto-parks off-screen; press the hotkey again to slide it back.
- Drag the drawer's inner edge to resize width/height — it remembers for next time.
- Because it is its own window, one line of `collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .stationary]` makes it appear on every Space and over full-screen apps — no Finder, Apple Events, or private SPI.

## Inside the drawer

- Sidebar: Finder's own sidebar, read the way Finder shows it: Favorites in Finder's order, iCloud Drive, Locations (eject buttons; updates on mount and unmount) and Tags (click to list tagged files via Spotlight; folded at first). Settings › Sidebar turns items on and off, or "Same as Finder" follows Finder's own sidebar settings, re-read each time the drawer opens.
- Menu bar icon: click toggles the drawer; right-click (or Control-click) opens the menu.
- File list: an AppKit NSOutlineView list view with Name / Size / Kind / Date Modified, click-to-sort headers, Group by Kind, folders that expand in place, and Finder's shortcuts: Return renames, ⌘↓ / ⌘O open, ⌘⌫ trashes, ⌘[ ⌘] ⌘↑ navigate, ⌘F searches (this folder or subfolders), ⌘⇧. shows hidden files, Space / ⌥Space Quick Look.
- Live updates via FSEvents; refreshes keep expansion, selection and scroll position.
- Drag and drop in and out (list, folder rows, sidebar, path bar); moves within a volume, copies across, never overwrites.
- Settings: language, appearance, accent, launch at login, default edge, auto-park, mouse side buttons, shortcut recorder with conflict checks, Full Disk Access status, update check.
- Six languages: Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese.

## Why its own window

The original direction was to avoid rebuilding a file browser UI by driving a real Finder window via AppleScript + Accessibility. That worked but cost a lot: per-Space window juggling, cross-Space moves blocked under SIP, private SkyLight/CGS SPI, telling "our" windows from the user's, timestamp-guessing for auto-park. Switching to its own window removed all of it — at the cost of building the browser UI with NSOutlineView (the component behind Finder's list view), which gets very close while keeping the architecture far cleaner.

## Install notes

- Homebrew: `brew install --cask rocavence/tap/findly`
- Self-signed (not Apple-notarized). On first launch, open via right-click → Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Findly.app`.
- Full Disk Access: the drawer browses the whole file system and the sidebar mirrors Finder favorites. Grant it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Without it, TCC-protected folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, CloudStorage/Dropbox) can't be opened; the drawer explains why and links to the settings pane.
- Tested on macOS 14+, primarily macOS 26 (Tahoe).
- Tech stack: Swift 6, AppKit (NSPanel, NSOutlineView), SwiftUI settings, FSEvents, NSMetadataQuery, Quick Look, Carbon RegisterEventHotKey, XcodeGen.
